overview: Porthgwarra is a tiny, hidden cove between Land’s End and Porthcurno, at the end of a narrow lane off the B3283 near St Levan. There’s a small sandy beach, a slipway, a café and a few cottages, and that’s about it, which is exactly its charm.

Look for the tunnels at the foot of the slipway: one was dug by St Just tin miners so farmers could bring horses and carts down to collect seaweed for their fields, and another gave fishermen access to the sea.

expect.title: The cove
expect.text: A small sandy beach and slipway between granite cliffs, safe for swimming inside the cove.

expect.title: Miners’ tunnels
expect.text: Tunnels cut through the rock at the bottom of the slipway, a reminder of the cove’s working past.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: Walk to Porthcurno in about 45 minutes, or to Land’s End in about an hour and a half.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: A car park in the village, a small shop and café, and public toilets.

goodToKnow.label: Private cove
goodToKnow.text: The cove and slipway are privately owned; visitors are welcome to enjoy them quietly and respectfully.

goodToKnow.label: Swimming
goodToKnow.text: Stay inside the cove: beyond the headland there are strong, dangerous currents.

week.text: A peaceful stop on a far-west day, and a starting point for one of the most scenic stretches of the coast path. Combine it with Porthcurno and the Minack.

pairWith.why: the bigger beach along the path

tips: The lane down is narrow: take it slowly and expect to reverse for oncoming cars.
